title: Continuous maps and derivations of completed polynomial local rings
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $r\geq0$, let $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]_{\mathfrak q}$ for a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of the polynomial ring, and write $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak qP$ and $S=\varprojlim_nP/\mathfrak p^n$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The module $\Omega^1_{P/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is free on $\mathrm dx_1,\ldots,\mathrm dx_r$. Its completion is the free $S$-module $F=S^{\oplus r}$, with the unique continuous derivation $\widehat d:S\to F$ extending $d:P\to\Omega^1_{P/k}$. Let $B$ be a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra and $f:S\to B$ a continuous local $k$-map [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For every finitely generated $B$-module $M$ with its maximal-ideal-adic topology (finite means generated by finitely many elements), composition with $\widehat d$ is a $B$-linear bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(F\otimes_SB,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Der}^{\mathrm{cont}}_k(S,M).$$
The action of $S$ on $M$ on the right is through $f$, and a derivation is additive, vanishes on $k$, and satisfies $D(ab)=f(a)D(b)+f(b)D(a)$. Moreover, for every complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra $E$, restriction gives a bijection from continuous local $k$-maps $S\to E$ to local $k$-maps $P\to E$. If $E\twoheadrightarrow B$ is a surjective local $k$-map with square-zero kernel, every such $f$ has a continuous local lift $S\to E$. Neither the residue field of $P$ nor that of $B$ is required to equal $k$ or to be separable over $k$.

source.place: Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion), completion and continuity argument, and Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous). Continuous-derivation clause is the localized polynomial calculation: D(p^n) is contained in p^(n-1) times the differential module; extend to inverse limits. No coefficient-field splitting is used.

proof.text: Put $A=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and let $c:P\to S$ be the completion map. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to $k\to A$ and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to $A\to P$. Thus $P$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak p$ is finitely generated. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $S$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak pS$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] with module $P$, the coordinate map $S\to P/\mathfrak p^n$ is onto with kernel $\mathfrak n^n$, for every $n\geq1$. In particular $c(P)$ is dense, and the inverse-limit topology on $S$ is its maximal-ideal-adic topology.

By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], $\Omega_{A/k}$ is free on $\mathrm dx_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] to the multiplicative set $A\setminus\mathfrak q$ to get $\Omega_{P/k}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^rP\,\mathrm dx_i$. Taking quotients and compatible sequences coordinatewise identifies its completion with $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^rS\,e_i$: a finite tuple of compatible sequences is the same as a compatible sequence of finite tuples. This is the specified identification, sending $\mathrm dx_i$ to $e_i$.

Compose $d:P\to\Omega_{P/k}$ with each coordinate of this basis to obtain $k$-derivations $\partial_i:P\to P$, with $\partial_i(x_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends](1) with $I=\mathfrak p$, obtaining $\widehat\partial_i:S\to S$. Its explicit formula uses the $(n+1)$st input coordinate for the $n$th output coordinate. Hence it sends $\mathfrak n^{n+1}$ into $\mathfrak n^n$ by the kernel description of Step 1 and is continuous. It vanishes on $k$, since every coordinate of the extension on $k$ is zero. Set $\widehat d(s)=\sum_i\widehat\partial_i(s)e_i$. This is a continuous $k$-derivation extending $d$ into $F$. Uniqueness follows from density: for any other continuous extension and any $s\in S$, choose $a_N\in P$ with $c(a_N)\equiv s\pmod{\mathfrak n^N}$. The two values agree modulo every $\mathfrak n^nF$ by continuity. Their difference is zero, since each coordinate of $F=S^r$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), part (1), with its explicit shifted-coordinate formula

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak m$ for the maximal ideal of $B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] to $(B,\mathfrak m,M)$. The map $\widehat B\otimes_BM\to\varprojlim_nM/\mathfrak m^nM$ sends $1\otimes z$ to $(z\bmod\mathfrak m^nM)_n$ and is an isomorphism. As $B\to\widehat B$ is an isomorphism by the assumed completeness, this proves that the canonical map $M\to\varprojlim_nM/\mathfrak m^nM$ is an isomorphism. In particular $M$ is separated. No completeness of $M$ for the smaller ideal $f(\mathfrak n)B$ is asserted or used.

A $B$-linear map $u:F\otimes_SB\to M$ is specified uniquely by $m_i=u(e_i\otimes1)$: the tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identify $F\otimes_SB$ with $B^r$ by $e_i\otimes b\mapsto b e_i$. Its composite with $\widehat d$ is $D_u(s)=\sum_i f(\widehat\partial_i(s))m_i$. Additivity, vanishing on $k$ and the Leibniz identity follow term by term. It is continuous: $f(\mathfrak n^n)\subseteq\mathfrak m^n$ because $f$ is local, and $\widehat d(\mathfrak n^{n+1})\subseteq\mathfrak n^nF$ by Step 3. Thus $D_u(\mathfrak n^{n+1})\subseteq\mathfrak m^nM$.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property; explicit coordinate calculation using Steps 1-3

proof.text: Conversely let $D:S\to M$ be a continuous $k$-derivation and set $m_i=D(c(x_i))$. Restrict along $c$; the universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and the basis in Step 2 imply that this restriction is the unique derivation on $P$ with those $r$ values. Therefore $D$ and $D_u$ of Step 5 agree on $c(P)$. For $s\in S$ choose $a_N\in P$ as in Step 3. For each $n$, continuity of both additive maps gives $D(s)-D_u(s)\in\mathfrak m^nM$ by choosing $N$ sufficiently large. Step 4 implies equality. Thus evaluation at the $x_i$ is inverse to $u\mapsto D_u$. Both maps commute with addition and multiplication by $b\in B$, since these operations multiply or add the coordinates $m_i$. This proves precisely the claimed $B$-linear bijection.

source.place: Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), and the density argument of Steps 1 and 4

proof.text: Let $E$ be a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak l$, and $h:P\to E$ a local $k$-map. Since $h(\mathfrak p^n)\subseteq\mathfrak l^n$, it induces compatible maps $h_n:P/\mathfrak p^n\to E/\mathfrak l^n$. For $s=(s_n)_n\in S$, define $\widehat h(s)$ as the unique element of $E=\varprojlim_nE/\mathfrak l^n$ whose $n$th coordinate is $h_n(s_n)$. Coordinatewise addition and multiplication show it is a $k$-algebra map extending $h$. Step 1 gives $\widehat h(\mathfrak n^n)\subseteq\mathfrak l^n$, proving continuity and locality: its residue map is the field map induced by $h$, so the inverse image of $\mathfrak l$ is $\mathfrak n$. Any continuous extension is equal to it by approximating $s$ by $c(a_N)$ and using $\bigcap_n\mathfrak l^n=0$. Conversely the restriction of a continuous local map is local, since $c^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak p$. These are inverse operations.

source.place: Section 00M9 (section-completion); coordinate construction of the extension, with completeness and the kernels of Step 1

proof.text: Finally write $\pi:E\twoheadrightarrow B$ and $J=\ker\pi$, so $J^2=0$. Choose $y_i\in E$ with $\pi(y_i)=f(c(x_i))$. The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives $g:A\to E$, $x_i\mapsto y_i$. Every $t\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ has unit image in $B$, hence $g(t)$ is a unit in $E$: lift the inverse to $v\in E$, write $g(t)v=1+j$, and use $(1+j)^{-1}=1-j$. The fraction formula $h(a/t)=g(a)g(t)^{-1}$ therefore defines $h:P\to E$; it is well defined by the equality rule for fractions of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], since $u(at'-a't)=0$ with $g(u)$ a unit gives $g(a)g(t')=g(a')g(t)$. It satisfies $\pi h=f c$ and is local. Indeed $J$ consists of nilpotents and is contained in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak l$ of $E$; since $E/J\cong B$, one has $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak l$. Consequently $h^{-1}(\mathfrak l)=(fc)^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak p$. Step 7 extends $h$ to a continuous local $\widehat h:S\to E$. The maps $\pi\widehat h$ and $f$ agree on $c(P)$ and are continuous (the local map $\pi$ sends $\mathfrak l^n$ into $\mathfrak m^n$), so they agree on $S$ by separation of $B$. This is the required lift. All arguments also work for $r=0$, and none chooses a residue-field section.

source.place: Polynomial universal property; elementary square-zero inverse formula in the proof of Tag 04EG (lemma-localization-formally-etale); Step 7

proof_origin.place: Localized polynomial calculation using Algebra Tags 00RX, 00RT, 05GG and 00MA and More on Algebra Tag 07PE; direct coordinate construction of continuous maps and square-zero lifts, consistent with Tags 07ED and 07NJ.
